gloss: I messed up, I screwed up

definitions.gloss: I messed up, I screwed up, I blew it
definitions.explanation: A casual exclamation acknowledging that one has made a significant mistake or blunder. Past tense of やらかす, almost always used in this past form to react to something that has already gone wrong.

examples.japanese: やらかした！{鍵|かぎ}を{中|なか}に{忘|わす}れた。
examples.english: I messed up! I left my keys inside.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}なメールを{間違|まちが}えて{送|おく}っちゃった。やらかした。
examples.english: I accidentally sent an important email to the wrong person. I really messed up.

examples.japanese: 「どうしたの？」「{寝坊|ねぼう}してやらかした。{会議|かいぎ}に{遅刻|ちこく}した」
examples.english: "What happened?" "I overslept and screwed up. I was late for the meeting."

notes:
やらかした is the past tense of やらかす (to mess up, to commit a blunder). The base form やらかす exists but is far less common in everyday speech — the past form やらかした is the standard way this word appears, used as a reactive exclamation after realizing a mistake.

USAGE:
- Self-directed: やらかした！ (I messed up!)
- About someone else: あいつ、またやらかしたよ (That guy screwed up again)
- The mistake is usually significant or embarrassing, not a trivial slip

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- やっちゃった: lighter tone, "oops" — suitable for minor mistakes
- しまった: "oh no" — a broader expression of regret
- やらかした: implies a bigger, more consequential blunder

REGISTER:
Casual. Not appropriate in formal or business settings. In polite speech, {失敗|しっぱい}しました or ミスしました would be used instead.
